rv.q: All In may not be a full dramatic meal, but it’s a tasty treat for the run-up to Valentine’s Day, sweet and tart as a candy heart.
The event has been shaped by the A-list director Alex Timbers (“Moulin Rouge!”) into a largely satisfying whole.
Despite the wild characters and imaginative leaps, the humor is laidback, pleasant, and effortless, more likely to elicit warm smiles than thigh-slappers.
Comedy is risky business, but Simon Rich's starry 'All In: Comedy About Love' is a safer bet.
But this new production is a slight affair that’s as easy to forget as it is to watch.
It’s got a simple center, with some fun and some heart to it, but the commercial stunt of the whole endeavor is pointed and unavoidable.
Each cutesy bit is more self-satisfied and twee than the next.
The 90-minute All In is a perfect holiday snickerdoodle, a light and tasty snack no less funny for its brevity.
Despite the stories’ wryness and arch wit, Rich ultimately seems a sunny-eyed idealist—not just about individuals, but also in how we should treat each other.

Both earnest and naughty — and evocative, in its tone and subject matter, of something you would hear on NPR, another good reference point for the show — it’s a fitting topper for a clever confection that, in the end, doesn’t overstay its welcome.
It takes a starry cast to breathe life into the zany stories of All In, currently hampered as an armchair-seated concept rather than a fleshed-out show.

But despite the efforts of director Alex Timbers to lend theatricality to the evening via atmospheric sound and lighting effects, All In: Comedy About Love wears out its welcome before its conclusion despite its brief 90-minute running time.
They are clearly intended to be humorous and thereby often succeed as amusing.
All In feels like a joke that goes on for too long and it doesn’t have the knee-slapping payoff to make it worth 90 minutes of your time.
Choose your stars wisely, don't expect too much, and you'll have a reasonably good time.
But there’s a gap between being game and being entertaining — especially at inflated Broadway prices.
